questions: If the bottom row becomes completely filled after some blocks have moved during a time step, does the removal of that row happen immediately before processing the remaining blocks in the same step or only at the start of the next time step?
When multiple blocks are in the same column and one block moves down, can it occupy a cell that was just vacated by another block moving down earlier in the same “bottom‑to‑top” processing order?
If a block is removed because its row was cleared, does it cease to exist for all subsequent queries regardless of its original index, or could it be re‑added later?
Are the coordinates (x, y) defined with y=1 being the bottommost row, and does the grid extend infinitely upward (i.e., there is no upper bound on y beyond the given initial positions)?

In the query “does block A_j exist at time T_j+0.5”, does “exist” mean the block has not been removed by a row‑clear operation, regardless of its current position, or does it also require the block to be present in the grid at that exact half‑integer time instant?

Is the order “from bottom to top” defined by increasing y‑coordinate, and if several blocks share the same y‑coordinate, is their relative order arbitrary or based on their x‑coordinate or original index?
When the bottom row is cleared, are all blocks in that row removed simultaneously, and does this removal affect the “bottom‑to‑top” processing of the remaining blocks in the same time step?

Are the values of T_j guaranteed to be within the simulation horizon (i.e., ≤ 10^100), and if a query asks for a time beyond the simulated steps, should we assume the process continues indefinitely according to the same rules?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, in order from bottom to top, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j+0.5. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
